title: deg2rad
summary: Convert angles from degrees to radians in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Floating GPU inputs can participate in fusion. Typed integer and logical gpuArray extensions gather through their owning provider and restore a validated result to the same device when that owner can physically supply the required result precision; otherwise the call rejects instead of silently narrowing.

description: `r = deg2rad(d)` converts each angle in `d` from degrees to radians using `d*pi/180`, with element-wise behavior matching MATLAB and RunMat.
behaviors: Operates element-wise on scalars, vectors, matrices, and N-D tensors.

MATLAB documents single and double input. RunMat extension mode additionally accepts logical input and integer values that are exactly representable as double; inexact wide integers are rejected rather than rounded.
Complex inputs are scaled component-wise, matching ordinary multiplication by `pi/180`.
Single and complex-single inputs preserve single precision.
Output shape matches the input shape.
String inputs are unsupported and raise a builtin-scoped error.

faqs.question: Is `deg2rad(x)` equivalent to `x*pi/180`?
faqs.answer: Yes. The builtin exists for readability and MATLAB compatibility.

faqs.question: Does `deg2rad` preserve array shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each element is converted independently and the original shape is preserved.
